title: Should I Have Expressed a Different Intent? Counterfactual Generation for LLM-Based Autonomous Control
claim: A user-agent-environment closed loop can be formalized as a causal model, enabling counterfactual queries about alternative user intents.
layout: 3 panels: large concrete example on top, two abstract loops below; factual vs counterfactual
description: The figure has three panels. Panel (a), the top half, is a concrete example. A network operator sits at a desk with three monitors on the left, an LLM block with the ChatGPT, Meta and Mistral logos is in the middle, and a network topology of computers, a router, a base station and a laptop is on the right. Numbered circles 1–4 mark arrows that carry the prompt 'Configure gNB to maximize throughput', a code snippet for the action, an XML-style KPI feedback snippet, and the text report back to the operator. Panels (b) and (c) are the bottom row. Each is a row of three boxes (User, LLM agent, Environment/Simulation) joined by double arrows. (b) is labeled with the factual variables Prompt X, Action A, Feedback Z and Report Y. (c) repeats the same layout with counterfactual variables X', A_X'(T), Z_X'(T) and Y_X'(T). The eye goes first to the illustrated operator and the numbered loop.
caption: (a) Example of the agentic framework studied in this work: A network operator provides an intent as a prompt to an LLM-based agent. The agent translates this prompt into an action, which is used to configure the network. The network executes the action, and returns environment feedback to the LLM in the form of KPIs, which the LLM processes and summarizes into a report for the operator. (b) LLM-environment interaction model: The user provides a prompt X, which the LLM maps to an action A. The environment executes action A and produces feedback Z. The LLM then combines (X, A, Z) to generate the response Y , which is returned to the user. (c) Given a factual episode T = (X, A, Z, Y ), the network operator chooses a counterfactual prompt X′. Given an observed factual episode T = (X, A, Z, Y ), our goal is to estimate the counterfactual report YX′(T) that the user would have received, under the same conditions, had the input prompt been X′ ∈E(X) instead of X (see Fig. 2 for an example).
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-powered agents can translate high-level user intents into plans and actions in an environment. Yet after observing an outcome, users may wonder: What if I had phrased my intent differently? We introduce a framework that enables such counterfactual reasoning in agentic LLM-driven control scenarios, while providing formal reliability guarantees. Our approach models the closed-loop interaction between a user, an LLM-based agent, and an environment as a structural causal model (SCM), and leverages test-time scaling to generate multiple candidate counterfactual outcomes via probabilistic abduction. Through an offline calibration phase, the proposed conformal counterfactual generation (CCG) yields sets of counterfactual outcomes that are guaranteed to contain the true counterfactual outcome with high probability. We showcase the performance of CCG on a wireless network control use case, demonstrating significant advantages compared to naive re-execution baselines.
